fichas.title: Subsidiary and storage areas for experimental theatres
fichas.summary: Open-stage theatres need subsidiary areas for scenery, platforms, and stands, together with storage space. The subsidiary areas should match the stage in size; the text states that subsidiary areas plus storage amount to about 30% of the total area. Open stages use less scenery because they are viewed from many sides and safety regulations restrict scenery.
uses: Provide support space for open-stage productions

fichas.title: Storage for large stages
fichas.summary: Large-stage storage accommodates scenery, backdrops, furniture, props, costumes, and related items. Scenery stores should be at stage level and immediately adjacent to the stage, with access routes and openings planned for scenery height and fire protection. Storage needs depend on repertoire and production frequency; the text describes traditional backdrop storage and container-based, computer-controlled storage systems.

fichas.title: Costume storage and hanging systems
fichas.summary: Costume-storage requirements depend on the number of productions in the repertoire and the size of the ensemble, including chorus and ballet in opera. The page gives alternative storage measures per costume and per running metre of rail, and illustrates two-level and single-level fixed clothing storage.
